tasks.short: Monitor conveyor operation and maintain specified operating levels

steps.what: Check the authorized operating levels and alarm limits for the current conveyor and material
Observe lights, dials and gauges for operating-level deviations and malfunction indications
inputs: existing conveyor instrument readings and status signals

steps.what: Observe actual conveyor movement and physical conditions not established by instrument readings
outputs: operator's physical observations and confirmed limitations of instrument indications

steps.what: Determine whether an authorized adjustment or stop is needed and select the exact control and setting
inputs: operator's physical observations and confirmed limitations of instrument indications
outputs: operator-selected exact control action or decision to retain setting

steps.what: Apply only the selected authorized control action when needed
inputs: operator-selected exact control action or decision to retain setting
outputs: operator-applied control action or unchanged setting

tasks.design: Configure the existing instrument view in {OPS_SYSTEM} to highlight out-of-limit readings using approved limits. The operator still checks physical conveyor behavior and chooses and applies every control action; the view has read-only authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Continuous scanning of separate existing readings can obscure a developing deviation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native control-system views can highlight threshold breaches on signals already instrumented.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting jams or mechanical trouble not represented reliably by a signal.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile actual machine behavior with instrument indications.

ambition.what: Improve instrument visibility without autonomous conveyor control.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: industrial control displays can highlight existing readings against configured limits; physical inspection and authorized control decisions remain distinct work.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing conveyor control and instrument display. Existing sensors produce the readings; approved specifications provide limits checked in s1. No new sensor capture, model inference or automatic control is assumed.

Native display configuration first, limited to already reliable signals. No separate notification or malfunction record is produced here; escalation and production recording are separate task instances.
Shares are provisional, not measured. Gross 12 minus 1 threshold/view upkeep gives 11 net. Control-button time is 1% fully retained; machine runtime is not a labor saving.
unknowns: Which signals already exist and whether highlighting already operates
research_questions: Can observed gauge-scanning time be reduced while preserving detection of physical faults?

already_counted.description: Check highlighted readings and instrument limitations

incremental.description: Review display limits and nuisance indications

approvals.approved_version: exact control and setting selected at end of s4; changed condition requires a fresh selection

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native highlighting is already adequate; cautious range below provisional 11% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify packages and inspect packaging quality on conveyors

steps.what: Identify packages from actual labels or existing package identifiers as they pass the inspection point
Inspect moving packages for visible damage, closure defects and other applicable packaging faults
Determine whether each observed package meets quality criteria or requires the local exception procedure

tasks.design: Retain visual package inspection using existing identity information in {OPS_SYSTEM}. A package identifier establishes identity, not packaging condition; no camera coverage, defect dataset or reliable automatic rejection capability is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visible defects vary with package orientation, material and conveyor conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced new inspection input is available in this task scenario.
tasks.still_hard: Recognizing actual faults while avoiding false defect calls.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret borderline packaging condition in context.

ambition.what: No unsupported automatic packaging quality decision.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: package identification and visual packaging inspection are distinct; a barcode alone cannot establish physical packaging quality.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing package identity view. Actual labels produce identification; the operator produces observed condition. Existing scanning assistance is already present and earns no new saving.

Inspection itself establishes no separate report, send or record-writing baseline. If a local quality record is required, map its actual authoring and commit before estimating it; do not invent administration inside this observation task.
Native identity display considered first. All three steps remain; provisional shares are not measurements and net saving is zero.
unknowns: Available camera coverage, defect definitions and any actual local inspection record requirement
research_questions: Observe whether package identification or an actual quality record involves duplicated entry; can existing inputs establish defects reliably?

already_counted.description: Inspect actual packaging and decide quality outcome

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to existing identification or physical inspection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record production data, equipment problems and downtime

steps.what: Check actual scale readings, production counts and current material specification for the reporting period
inputs: existing scale readings and counter values
outputs: source-checked weights, quantities and material types

steps.what: Identify actual storage locations and record observed equipment problems and downtime boundaries
inputs: actual stop and restart times or explicit unknowns
outputs: operator-entered locations, problem facts and downtime boundaries

steps.what: Populate and verify production fields from existing source values alongside the operator's location and problem entries
inputs: source-checked weights, quantities and material types
operator-entered locations, problem facts and downtime boundaries
approved units and record field mappings
outputs: completed production and equipment-performance record draft

steps.what: Check the complete record for correct period, material, units, location and honest downtime uncertainty
inputs: completed production and equipment-performance record draft
source-checked weights, quantities and material types
operator-entered locations, problem facts and downtime boundaries
outputs: final checked production and equipment-performance record

steps.what: Save the checked production record in the same reporting system
inputs: final checked production and equipment-performance record

tasks.design: Configure the native production record in {OPS_SYSTEM} to reuse existing scale, counter and run fields. The operator supplies actual storage destinations and malfunction details, checks the assembled record and saves it; missing data remains visibly unresolved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing numerical source values may be copied into a separate form within the reporting system.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record configuration can reuse source fields with explicit units and reporting periods.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing actual downtime boundaries and causes from imperfect observations.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a measured stop from an assumed malfunction cause.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native production forms can reuse existing scale and counter fields; location and fault facts require actual observations or existing verified sources.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is conveyor production and equipment reporting. Existing scales, counters and run specifications produce numerical and type fields; s2 explicitly captures actual location and fault/downtime facts, with its labor retained.
Native field reuse first. No new sensors, automatic cause inference, hidden structured-input capture or automated send. Already populated records receive no saving.
Shares are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Gross 20 minus 2 mapping upkeep gives 18 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained; review is counted separately from source capture.
unknowns: Source availability and actual duplicate entry burden
research_questions: Can native field reuse preserve units, material identity and reporting periods while reducing observed re-keying?

already_counted.description: Verify populated fields and the final production record

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings and inspect missing-value patterns

approvals.approved_version: final checked production record at end of s4; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if already populated; cautious range below provisional 18% net until duplicate entry is observed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inform supervisors about equipment malfunctions requiring attention

steps.what: Confirm the equipment identity, observed malfunction and current condition from the actual machine and available fault display
inputs: existing machine identity and fault indications
outputs: operator-confirmed malfunction facts and unresolved uncertainties

steps.what: Inform the supervisor by radio or phone about the malfunction, current condition and need for attention, and answer clarifying questions
inputs: operator-confirmed malfunction facts and unresolved uncertainties
outputs: supervisor informed of the malfunction and its known limitations

tasks.design: Retain the supervisor call using actual fault information from {OPS_SYSTEM}. Existing fault codes support the explanation, but a code does not replace describing the current machine condition or answering questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: A supervisor needs the actual malfunction context rather than an unexplained indication.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing fault displays already support identification; no additional communication saving is established.
tasks.human_edge: Answer questions about the actual equipment condition.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: operators commonly inform supervisors by voice using observed machine condition and available fault indications.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the conveyor fault display. The operator produces actual malfunction observations and reads identity before the call; no structured incident payload is invented.

This is a voice escalation scenario. No separate written message or record is established by the statement; production problem recording is explicitly a different task, not silently folded into the call.
Native fault display first. Source checking is split from conversation; neither changes. Shares are provisional and net saving is zero.
unknowns: Whether local escalation actually requires a separate written message or maintenance ticket
research_questions: Observe the escalation channel and split any actual message authoring and gated send before estimating it.

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual source checking and direct supervisor conversation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Controls and production administrators configure existing views and fields; the operator keeps control authority and fault communication.

role.ambitious_version: Reduce verified gauge scanning and repeated production entry while preserving physical inspection, control decisions and supervisor escalation.
